questions.topic: The gap from the subtonic to the raised leading tone

questions.stem: On the transit board, why is the gap between subtonic and leading tone smaller than a whole tone?

answer.exemplar: The subtonic is a whole tone below the tonic and the leading tone is a semitone below, so their gap is one semitone, smaller than a whole tone.

questions.explanation: A whole tone minus a semitone leaves a semitone gap. The written answer should state both distances.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The two directions of the melodic minor scale
questions.learningObjective: Explain why melodic minor differs by direction
questions.stem: On the transit board, why does melodic minor use different forms ascending and descending?

answer.exemplar: Ascending raises six and seven to gain a leading tone and smooth the line, while descending reverts to natural minor to avoid the awkward augmented second and descending awkwardness.

questions.explanation: The two forms balance leading-tone pull with smooth descent. The written answer should mention both directions.
questions.hint: Ascent gains a leading tone; descent smooths.
